function.arguments: {"research_topic":"Conduct a comprehensive, source-grounded reconstruction of the Internet Research Agency’s alleged 2016 United States social-media influence operation using only evidence available through benchmark tools. Locate and cite the benchmark source IDs for: (1) factual allegations in relevant United States Department of Justice indictments, clearly labeled as allegations; (2) findings, judgments, and confidence assessments in United States Senate materials, clearly distinguished from adjudicated facts; (3) platform-provided evidence from Facebook, Instagram, Twitter, YouTube, or other platforms concerning account identities or labels, content, activity dates, audiences, impressions or reach, advertising, and coordination; (4) identities, characteristics, roles, and relationships of known or alleged personas, organizations, and accounts; (5) funding sources, payment mechanisms, legal or organizational entities, employees or contractors, and operational infrastructure; and (6) apparent objectives, target audiences, narratives, tactics, timing, and intended or observed effects. Build an evidence matrix that distinguishes verified facts, allegations, assessments, inferences, and unresolved uncertainty. Do not invent or normalize entity names, account IDs, dates, relationships, causal claims, or metrics: use only identifiers and relationship names directly supported by returned sources. Every factual proposition must have one or more exact benchmark source IDs. Identify contradictions or limitations among sources, especially differences between platform metrics and Senate or DOJ descriptions. Return detailed research notes suitable for a final Markdown report and a JSON appendix with the required schema fields: findings (question, answer, supporting_entities, source_references), claims (claim, source_references), reasoning_steps (id, conclusion, premise_entities, premise_relations), and contradictions (contradiction_id, description, source_references)."}
function.name: ConductResearch
